{{nihongo|'''Isemikoto Shrine'''|伊勢命神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Oki Province]].

'''Isemikoto Shrine''' (いせみことじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|arz|اوكينوشيما|ceb|Okinoshima Chō|de|Okinoshima (Shimane)|es|Okinoshima (Shimane)|fa|اوکینوشیما، شیمانه|fr|Okinoshima|id|Okinoshima, Shimane|it|Okinoshima|ja|隠岐の島町|ko|오키노시마정|ms|Okinoshima, Shimane|my|အိုခိနိုရှိမမြို့၊ ရှိမနဲ|pl|Okinoshima|ru|Окиносима|sv|Okinoshima, Shimane|tl|Okinoshima, Shimane|tr|Okinoshima|ur|اوکینوشیما، شیمانے|zh|隱岐之島町|qid=Q1205039}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ar|منطقة أوكي (شيمانه)|ceb|Oki-gun|es|Distrito de Oki|fr|District d'Oki|hu|Oki körzet|id|Distrik Oki, Shimane|it|Distretto di Oki|ja|隠岐郡|ko|오키군|pl|Powiat Oki|pt|Distrito de Oki|simple|Oki District, Shimane|zh|隱岐郡|qid=Q735735}}, {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|Q132751|qid=Q132751}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}) recorded in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}' as "Isemikoto Shrine, Myojin-tai" in Ochi District of {{ill|Oki Province|cs|Provincie Oki|de|Provinz Oki|es|Provincia de Oki|fa|ولایت اوکی|fr|Province d'Oki|id|Provinsi Oki|it|Oki (provincia)|ja|隠岐国|ko|오키국|lt|Okio žemė|nl|Oki (provincie)|pt|Província de Oki|ru|Оки (провинция)|simple|Oki Province|sk|Oki (provincia)|sr|Провинција Оки|tr|Oki (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Окі|zh|隱岐國|zh_min_nan|Oki-kok|qid=Q1063829}}, and its modern-era rank was former {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. The shrine is at the northern end of {{ill|Dōgojima|be|Догадзіма|bg|Дого (Шимане)|ceb|Dōgo|de|Dōgo|fr|Dōgo-jima|id|Dōgojima|ja|島後|ko|도고섬|ru|Дого (остров)|sv|Dogo|zh|島後|qid=Q3623017}}.

=== Shrine name ===
From the '{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|qid=Q11659057}}' of {{ill|Kanbun (era)|es|Kanbun|fa|کانبون (دوره)|fr|Ère Kanbun|id|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|ko|간분|ru|Камбун (нэнго)|simple|Kanbun (era)|sr|Канбун (ера)|sv|Kanbun|tr|Kanbun (dönem)|zh|寬文|qid=Q1146228}} 7 ({{ill|1667|Q7588|qid=Q7588}}) onward, all writings call it "Naigū" or "Naigū Daimyōjin," and in the early modern period it came to be regarded almost as an offshoot of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|abstract|Q11581011|ja|皇大神宮|tok|tomo sewi suli Naku|zh|皇大神宮|qid=Q11581011|lt=Inner Shrine}} of Ise. However, old tradition survived, including naming the deity "Ise-no-Mikoto," so in {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} it reverted to "Isemikoto Shrine" following the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'.

=== Enshrined deity ===
*'''Ise-no-Mikoto'''
Although this deity is unique to Oki and not seen elsewhere, from the divine name and its relation to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Isobe}} it is thought to be a deity deeply connected to the Ise region through maritime people<ref name="白水社">'Nihon no Kamigami.'</ref>. There is also faith in its efficacy for {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=praying for rain}}<ref name="調査報告">'Shikinaisha Chōsa Hōkoku.'</ref>.

=== Origin ===
According to the transmission of the {{ill|Shake (social class)|Q11588367|qid=Q11588367}} family, when the Ise lineage first settled on Oki Island, a divine fire (mysterious fire) came nightly over the sea and stopped at Kariya, about 5.5 km southwest of the current site. They built a small {{ill|Hokora|Q1442984|qid=Q1442984|lt=shrine}} there and enshrined their ancestral deity '''Ise Myōjin'''; the fire ceased, and that shrine was later moved to the present site<ref name="調査報告"/>.

In the {{ill|Shōsōin Documents|ja|正倉院文書|ru|Тексты Тодайдзи|uk|Тексти Тодайдзі|qid=Q11545362}}, the '{{ill|Tenpyō|Q1199879|qid=Q1199879}} 4 ({{ill|732|Q23569|qid=Q23569}}) Oki Province tax register' records Isobe no Atae Mantoku as assistant district governor of Yakidō (Ochi) District. Also, though in {{ill|Dōzen|Q11476216|qid=Q11476216}}, a {{ill|Mokkan|Q4299994|qid=Q4299994|lt=Heijō-kyū mokkan}} bears the name Ishibe no Masaki of Chiburi district, showing Isobe/Ishibe groups existed in Oki. Isobe are regarded as the "Isebe" in the {{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}} ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}} section), established with the {{ill|Kaifu|Q446149|qid=Q446149}}. Both were occupational be-min involved in fishing and hunting, but while Ama-be were widely distributed mainly in western Japan, Isobe (Isebe) were widely distributed mainly in eastern Japan with Ise as base<ref>Ryō Ōta, 'Seishi Kakei Jisho' (Isobe Kōyōdō, 1920), and 'Seishi Kakei Daijiten Vol.1' (1934).</ref>. Since the name Ise is also said to derive from "iso" (shore/rock)<ref>Many persons surnamed Isobe/Ishibe also served in Ise Jingū rites.</ref>, links with Ise through Isobe are inferred. Especially because the {{ill|Isobe Clan|Q11588086|qid=Q11588086}} in Ochi District where this shrine stands seem to have been powerful enough to hold assistant district office, it is inferred that maritime groups headed by Isobe were involved in this shrine's founding<ref name="白水社"/>.

The shrine was known early to the center. '{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}}' ({{ill|Kashō|Q1373157|qid=Q1373157}} 1 / {{ill|848|Q30380|qid=Q30380}}, 11th month, day 16) says it was treated according to the precedent for "myōjin" due to repeated miracles. This is one of the few cases clearly stating why a shrine was ranked myojin-taisha in the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168}}<ref>Only 3 cases (4 shrines) state the reason: the case of Mishima-no-kami (now {{ill|Mishima Taisha|el|Μισίμα Τάισα|fr|Mishima-taisha|ja|三嶋大社|tr|Mishima Tapınağı|zh|三嶋大社|qid=Q650772}}) and Ikonahime-no-kami in {{ill|Izu Province|Q860928|qid=Q860928}}, and the case of Iyahiko-no-kami (now {{ill|Yahiko Shrine|Q195684|qid=Q195684}}) in {{ill|Echigo Province|be|Этыго (правінцыя)|ckb|پارێزگای ئێچیگۆ|cs|Provincie Ečigo|de|Provinz Echigo|es|Provincia de Echigo|fa|ولایت اچیگو|fr|Province d'Echigo|gl|Provincia de Echigo|id|Provinsi Echigo|it|Echigo|ja|越後国|ko|에치고국|lt|Ečigo žemė|nl|Echigo (provincie)|pt|Província de Echigo|ru|Этиго (провинция)|simple|Echigo Province|sk|Ečigo (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ечиго|tr|Echigo (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Етіґо|zh|越後國|zh_min_nan|Etigo-kok|zh_yue|越後國|qid=Q666514}}.</ref>. It was also one of the four major Oki shrines treated as kokuhei-taisha (myojin-taisha) in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engi system}}, but does not appear in Ochi District of the '{{ill|Izumi Province Divine Name Register|Q11420490|qid=Q11420490|lt=Oki no Kuni Jinmyōchō}}'<ref>That text has places in Ochi District where divine names are missing. Also, "Senior Fourth Upper Ise Myōjin" appears in neighboring {{ill|Suki district|Q10920245|qid=Q10920245}}, so it is also argued that it may have been recorded under another district for some reason (Mitsuhashi Ken, ed. annotation, 'Shintō Taikei: Jinja-hen, Sōki-jō,' 1986).</ref>.

From medieval times onward it was revered by warrior families, with known donations including paddy land named Aikushida by Omosu Kiyoshige in {{ill|Kanshō|Q1143928|qid=Q1143928}} 3 ({{ill|1462|Q6546|qid=Q6546}}), one {{ill|Tachi|Q120676|qid=Q120676}} dedicated by Sasaki Tamekiyo claiming the office of {{ill|Shugo|Q1141023|qid=Q1141023}} of Oki in {{ill|Genki (era)|Q1145064|qid=Q1145064}} 1 ({{ill|1570|Q6659|qid=Q6659}}), and mountain woodland donated by {{ill|Horio Yoshiharu|Q8190645|qid=Q8190645}}, lord of {{ill|Matsue Domain|Q1017072|qid=Q1017072}}, in {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 12 ({{ill|1607|Q6756|qid=Q6756}}). In the early modern period shrine land income was 2 {{ill|Koku|Q855048|qid=Q855048}}.

It was ranked gōsha in Meiji 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), and after the war joined {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}.

=== Rituals ===
* Annual festival (July 26) - {{ill|Kagura|Q1348260|qid=Q1348260}} is performed through the night, and a {{ill|Shinko-shiki|Q123907414|qid=Q123907414}} is held every other year. Years with procession are called "hon-matsuri," those without "ura-matsuri." Before Meiji the festival day was June 2; after adoption of the {{ill|Solar calendar|Q210953|qid=Q210953}} it was changed to July 16, then later to the current date.
* Kumi Kagura (July 26 or 25) - dedicated from the night of the annual festival in hon-matsuri years, and from the eve in ura-matsuri years. Designated as a national {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=selected intangible folk cultural property}} and a Shimane prefectural {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=intangible folk cultural property}} (see {{ill|Dōgo Kumi Kagura|Q11476336|qid=Q11476336}}).
Because place names near the shrine include Hōjōe-da, Aikushida, and Kagami-mochida, it is inferred that rites of {{ill|Ryobu Shinto|Q4402813|qid=Q4402813}} were once held here<ref name="調査報告"/>.

=== Priests ===
In ancient times it was likely held by people surnamed Ise or Isobe; since early modern times it has been inherited by the Hachiman family. In the early-Meiji 'Shimago Jinja Torishirabechō,' they are recorded with "family lineage generations unknown."
